stem: Which additional lesion type may be seen in more severe eczema?
explanation: Papules and vesicles may be seen in more severe eczema.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

rationale: Eczema is typically described as having dry skin, fine scale and poorly demarcated margins, with papules and vesicles appearing in more severe disease.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because more severe eczema may present with papules and vesicles.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because comedones and nodules are features of acne, not eczema.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because purpura and petechiae suggest bleeding into the skin, not eczema.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because target lesions are characteristic of erythema multiforme, not eczema.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because large tense bullae are not the typical additional lesions described in more severe eczema.
